ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #5
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The mother of your husband or wife is your (1 mark)
   A. mother-in-law
   B. sister-in-law
   C. ancestor
   D. care-giver

2. Articles: Choose the correct sentence. (1 mark)
   A. She has uncle an.
   B. She has a uncle.
   C. She has an uncle.
   D. She has the an uncle.

3. Which of these words has /r/ as its first sound? (1 mark)
   A. ribbon
   B. lake
   C. load
   D. light

4. Target sounds: Which word has the sound /aɪ/? (1 mark)
   A. invite
   B. farm
   C. noise
   D. turn

5. Poems and similes: Which sentence has a simile? (1 mark)
   A. The race started at nine.
   B. The runner won the race.
   C. The runner was as fast as a cheetah.
   D. The runner was tired.

6. Why did the woman say Neema's mother had taught her good manners? (1 mark)
   A. Because Neema spoke and acted politely
   B. Because Neema was rich
   C. Because Neema was late
   D. Because Neema was tall

7. 'He is old enough to ride a bicycle.' Here enough comes (1 mark)
   A. after the adjective
   B. before the verb
   C. at the end
   D. before the noun

8. In 'listen', the silent letter is (1 mark)
   A. n
   B. l
   C. t
   D. s

9. First aid is (1 mark)
   A. the last help
   B. a kind of food
   C. a road sign
   D. the first help given to a person who is hurt or ill

10. Which pronoun replaces 'Ali and I'? (1 mark)
   A. he
   B. you
   C. we
   D. they

11. What is the comparative of 'bad'? (1 mark)
   A. worst
   B. badder
   C. worse
   D. more bad

12. In the story shape, the highest point is (1 mark)
   A. the title
   B. the exciting part
   C. the last full stop
   D. the date

13. Which noun is uncountable? (1 mark)
   A. milk
   B. chair
   C. egg
   D. pupil

14. What are data bundles? (1 mark)
   A. An amount of internet you buy for a phone or computer
   B. A kind of laptop
   C. Bundles of firewood
   D. Sheets of paper

15. Which word begins with the sound /j/? (1 mark)
   A. giant
   B. zebra
   C. yellow
   D. jam

16. Which month is written correctly? (1 mark)
   A. September
   B. Septmber
   C. Septembre
   D. Septembar

17. Which sentence uses 'its' correctly to show belonging? (1 mark)
   A. I think its a goat.
   B. Its raining today.
   C. Its a fine day.
   D. The cow licked its calf.

18. Which sentence would best begin a narrative about a farm visit? (1 mark)
   A. The farm is nice.
   B. Last Saturday, my class visited a farm near our school.
   C. Farms grow food.
   D. I like cows.

19. In the story, why was Omondi standing alone? (1 mark)
   A. Other children refused to play with him because of his mother's illness
   B. He had a football
   C. He wanted to study
   D. He had lost his shoes

20. What does an adverb tell us? (1 mark)
   A. The name of a place
   B. How many things there are
   C. A person's name
   D. More about a verb, such as how, when or where

21. Which sentence uses the right word for how she sings? (1 mark)
   A. She sing well.
   B. She sings goodly.
   C. She sings good.
   D. She sings well.

22. What is a riddle? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of song
   B. A list of rules
   C. A long story
   D. A word puzzle that describes something without naming it

23. What is inferring the meaning of a word? (1 mark)
   A. Working out its meaning from the words around it
   B. Spelling it backwards
   C. Copying it
   D. Ignoring it

24. Who is a coach? (1 mark)
   A. A person who trains a team
   B. The person who sells kit
   C. The person who blows the whistle
   D. The team's fans

25. Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'apart, not together'? (1 mark)
   A. separete
   B. seperate
   C. separate
   D. seprate

26. What does 'A stitch in time saves nine' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Sewing is always fun
   B. Time is money
   C. Nine stitches are better than one
   D. Fixing a small problem early prevents a bigger one

27. Which words rhyme? (1 mark)
   A. clean and sweep
   B. tree and tall
   C. green and clean
   D. green and grass

28. Which sentence uses the past perfect? (1 mark)
   A. I had finished before he came.
   B. I am finishing.
   C. I have finished.
   D. I finish.

29. Which is the past participle of 'break'? (1 mark)
   A. broke
   B. breaked
   C. breaking
   D. broken

30. What is a salary? (1 mark)
   A. Money lost
   B. A school fee
   C. Money paid to a worker regularly
   D. Money borrowed from a bank

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Give two safety rules for using the internet. (2 marks)

32. Give the meaning of four words from the lesson: injury, treatment, painkiller, poison. (4 marks)

33. Change to the past progressive: 'The children are singing in the hall.' (2 marks)

34. Write a short talk of four sentences on how to care for a sick friend. (4 marks)

35. Explain what the saying 'A stitch in time saves nine' teaches. (2 marks)

36. Write a narrative of about 60 words about a visit to a farm. Include a beginning, a middle, an end and a simile. (5 marks)

37. Change these adjectives into adverbs: gentle, angry, quick. (3 marks)

38. Give two pieces of advice for staying safe online. (3 marks)

39. Correct the spellings: peple, libary, beutiful. (3 marks)

40. Explain two ways to make a story interesting. (4 marks)

41. Describe the steps to fill in a form correctly. (4 marks)

42. Write an invitation of three sentences to a wedding or birthday party, using 'invite' and 'decorate'. (3 marks)

43. Describe how to make the sounds /f/ and /v/ and say how they are different. Give one example pair. (4 marks)

44. List three things a child must never give to a stranger online. (3 marks)

45. Explain when we use some and when we use any. Give an example of each. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #5 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — mother-in-law
   The mother of your husband or wife is your mother-in-law.

2. C — She has an uncle.
   Uncle starts with a vowel sound, so we use an.

3. A — ribbon
   Ribbon starts with /r/.

4. A — invite
   Invite has /aɪ/ in its second syllable.

5. C — The runner was as fast as a cheetah.
   It compares the runner with a cheetah using as ... as.

6. A — Because Neema spoke and acted politely
   Her actions showed good manners.

7. A — after the adjective
   With adjectives, enough comes after the adjective.

8. C — t
   We say lisn, so the t is silent.

9. D — the first help given to a person who is hurt or ill
   First aid is given before a doctor takes over.

10. C — we
   We includes the speaker and another person.

11. C — worse
   Bad, worse, worst.

12. B — the exciting part
   Events rise to an exciting part.

13. A — milk
   We cannot count milk one by one.

14. A — An amount of internet you buy for a phone or computer
   Data bundles are bought to use the internet.

15. C — yellow
   'Yellow' begins with /j/, the y sound. 'Jam' and 'giant' begin with /ʤ/.

16. A — September
   September is spelt with a capital S and the ending -ber.

17. D — The cow licked its calf.
   'Its' without an apostrophe shows belonging.

18. B — Last Saturday, my class visited a farm near our school.
   It says when, who and where.

19. A — Other children refused to play with him because of his mother's illness
   The other children were afraid because they did not know the facts.

20. D — More about a verb, such as how, when or where
   Adverbs answer how, when and where.

21. D — She sings well.
   'Well' is the adverb; 'good' is an adjective.

22. D — A word puzzle that describes something without naming it
   The listener guesses the answer.

23. A — Working out its meaning from the words around it
   Context gives clues.

24. A — A person who trains a team
   A coach trains players.

25. C — separate
   Remember 'a rat' in separate.

26. D — Fixing a small problem early prevents a bigger one
   Early action saves later work.

27. C — green and clean
   'Green' and 'clean' end with the same sound.

28. A — I had finished before he came.
   Had + past participle.

29. D — broken
   Break, broke, broken.

30. C — Money paid to a worker regularly
   A salary is a regular payment for work.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: Do not share personal details; tell an adult if something worries you; use approved sites.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Injury: harm done to the body. Treatment: care given to a sick person. Painkiller: medicine that reduces pain. Poison: something that can make you very ill or kill you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: The children were singing in the hall.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for were, 1 mark for keeping singing.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: A greeting, two caring actions such as visiting and listening, and a closing thank-you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of the four parts.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: It teaches us to fix a small problem early, before it becomes a big problem.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fixing early and 1 mark for avoiding a bigger problem.

36. (5 marks)
   Answer: A story of about 60 words in the past tense with clear parts and a simile.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the beginning, 1 for events in order, 1 for the end, 1 for a simile, 1 for correct tense and punctuation.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: gently, angrily, quickly
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not give your name, school or address to strangers. Show worrying messages to a trusted adult. Ask a parent or teacher before opening a new page.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct piece of advice, up to 3.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: people, library, beautiful
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: Start with something that makes the reader curious, and add small details or similes. These help the reader picture the story and want to continue.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each way explained.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Read the whole form and its instructions, get the facts ready, write neatly in the spaces using block letters if asked, fill every space, check the spelling and sign if needed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: I invite you to my sister's wedding on Saturday. We will decorate the hall with flowers. Please come at ten o'clock.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Touch the top teeth to the lower lip and blow. /f/ is whispered and /v/ is voiced with a buzz. Example: fan and van.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the mouth position, 1 mark for /f/ whispered, 1 mark for /v/ voiced, 1 mark for the pair.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Name, home address, school name, password.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each, up to 3.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Some is used in positive sentences and polite offers: I have some books. Any is used in questions and negatives: Do you have any books?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule and 1 mark for each example.
